title: Keep a control version
intro: A canary deploys a candidate to limited traffic while the current version remains as a control. The comparison must influence the rollout decision.
takeaway: A slow rollout alone is not an evaluation. Define which outcomes will cause promotion, pause or abort.

beats.text: Version 1 is serving the application. Version 2 is a candidate change.
Keep the current version as a control. It gives the candidate a comparison.
Send limited traffic to the candidate. Observe its behavior before expanding.
Compare results from both versions. The result must change a rollout decision.

title: Limit the exposure
intro: In this example, the candidate receives ten percent of traffic: 1,000 of 10,000 requests. The other 9,000 stay on the current version.
takeaway: The percentages describe this illustrative window. A small share limits exposure, but can still harm affected users.

beats.text: This window has 10,000 requests. The candidate receives a ten-percent share.
9,000 requests go to version 1. Most traffic stays on the control.
1,000 requests go to version 2. The candidate has limited exposure.
Measure each version separately. A small rollout is not proof of safety.

title: An average hides failure
intro: Forty candidate exports fail. Everything else succeeds. Across all traffic that is 40 out of 10,000, or 0.4%, but the affected operation is much worse.
takeaway: Aggregate rates can conceal failures concentrated in a small version-and-operation slice.

beats.text: There are 10,000 total requests. Only 100 are exports handled by v2.
Forty candidate exports fail. The other requests succeed.
Overall: 40 failures out of 10,000. The headline error rate is only 0.4%.
An overall 1% alert would stay quiet. Split the results before judging safety.

title: Compare the same operation
intro: Compare export requests on the candidate with export requests on the control. Candidate exports fail 40 out of 100 times; control exports fail zero out of 900.
takeaway: The 40% candidate-export failure rate is relevant to this rollout. These authored counts are not real benchmark results.

beats.text: Compare exports with exports. Do not mix them with unrelated requests.
Version 1: zero failures out of 900. Control exports have a 0% error rate.
Version 2: 40 failures out of 100. Candidate exports have a 40% error rate.
The candidate has a clear regression. The comparison argues against promotion.

title: Abort and verify recovery
intro: After detecting the regression, stop sending new traffic to the candidate and verify the current version can safely resume the load.
takeaway: Rerouting new requests does not undo completed writes or guarantee schema compatibility. Rollback safety needs separate planning.

beats.text: The candidate fails the release check. Stop increasing its share.
Route new requests to the control. The candidate receives no new traffic.
Check the recovered service behavior. Do not assume abort means healthy.
Confirm recovery before concluding. Data changes may need separate repair.
